concerns.text: The headline equivalence claim (SC-003/SC-004, ≤15% gap vs PhysisForcing via TOST) is not methodologically supported. The filtered model is a ≈50M distilled 3D-U-Net trained at 64×64 on ~96 videos, while the PhysisForcing baseline is its PUBLISHED scores from a different architecture/scale. Any gap (or equivalence) is confounded by model capacity, resolution, and training data volume, not the filter. research.md admits this is 'associational/external', yet SC-003/SC-004 still frame TOST against the baseline as the decision criterion. The valid causal comparison is filtered vs unfiltered (same model); the plan should make that the primary TOST and demote the PhysisForcing gap to descriptive.

The TOST/Wilcoxon-Signed-Rank design never states the UNIT of observation. Wilcoxon-Signed-Rank is a PAIRED test — paired on what? Per-video scores from the filtered vs unfiltered models require the models to GENERATE videos (US-2 scenario 2: 'generates at least 64 new videos'), but no task in the plan generates videos from the trained models; T10 only 'evaluates' them. Without a generation step producing ≥64 videos per model, there are no per-sample scores to run TOST on, and n≥64 per condition is unachievable.

Construct validity of evaluation is unspecified: how are R-Bench and PAI-Bench scores computed for a 64×64 video-diffusion model's outputs? No task defines running these benchmarks (their harnesses, prompts, or scoring protocols), and the plan provides no evidence they accept arbitrary generated videos. Similarly, the Rapidata text-2-video human-preferences collection is a general prompt dataset — the plan does not verify it contains robotic-manipulation videos, which is the construct FR-001/US-1 name.

The curation rule is internally ambiguous: 'discard the bottom filter_discard_percent (default 40)' (a relative/percentile rule) and 'raw score < 60 / normalized < 0.60' (an absolute rule) are two DIFFERENT criteria that will discard different sets unless the 60th percentile of the pool happens to be exactly raw 60. The plan must pick one (or define precedence) or the filtered condition is not well-defined.

Power/construct concern: training a 50M-parameter video diffusion model for 10 epochs on ≤96 curated 64×64 videos on 2 CPU cores is very unlikely to produce a model whose generated videos are scoreable at all, making the downstream equivalence test vacuous. The plan needs a sanity gate (e.g., US-2 scenario 2's 80% MuJoCo pass rate) wired in as a go/no-go before TOST, or an acknowledgment of what a null result means.

FR-001/FR-010 mandate GENERATING videos with the Wan2.1 model; the plan substitutes acquisition of pre-existing Wan2.1 outputs from the Rapidata dataset. The plan itself concedes this 'should be reflected in the spec's assumption text' but the spec still says 'can be downloaded without requiring GPU resources for the generation step.' Until the spec FRs/assumptions are amended, the plan does not satisfy FR-001/FR-010 as written — kick back to spec for revision, then the plan is consistent.

US-2 scenario 2 requires the trained model to GENERATE at least 64 new videos with ≥80% passing the MuJoCo check (score ≥ 60th percentile of the initial uncurated batch). No plan task covers generating videos from the trained model or measuring this 80% pass rate; T9/T10 only score existing condition videos and compute benchmark scores. Either add a task or amend the spec.

'training loss decreases monotonically' is not covered by any task or success criterion — T7 records duration/RAM and NaN-loss retries only. Add a monotonic-loss check to T7 or the TrainedModel contract, or amend the spec.

concerns.location: research.md: Dataset Strategy table, Rapidata row; plan.md Summary step 1
concerns.text: The Rapidata text-2-video human-preferences (Wan2.1) collection is a general-purpose text-to-video preference dataset with diverse crowd prompts; it is not a robotic-manipulation video corpus. The research question (and FR-001, US-1) requires synthetic *robotic manipulation* videos. The plan asserts "exactly the construct FR-001/FR-019 require" without evidence the collection contains ≥128 robotic-manipulation videos. Either verify/filter the collection for manipulation content and state the expected yield, or identify a Wan2.1-output source that is manipulation-focused.

concerns.location: research.md: Dataset Strategy table, 'Wan2.1 reference assets' row (panopstor/wan21test ff7_wan21_dataset01.zip)
concerns.text: The designated top-up source for the n≥64 edge case is `panopstor/wan21test/ff7_wan21_dataset01.zip` — Final Fantasy VII fan-generated Wan2.1 clips. These are not robotic-manipulation videos and are inappropriate as additional training samples for this experiment. The top-up path must draw from manipulation-domain videos or the primary pool must be sized to avoid it.

concerns.location: research.md: Dataset Strategy table, PyBullet fixtures row (gym_pybullet_drones, pybullet_ring_task)
concerns.text: The PyBullet sanity-check fixtures are drone-flight and ring-task episodes, not robotic-manipulation contact scenarios; as "known-physics" fixtures for validating trajectory-continuity/contact-conservation scoring they are a partial fit at best. Note the domain mismatch or select manipulation-relevant fixtures.

Two conflicting VideoSample contracts exist. dataset_schema.schema.yaml requires `id`, `status` (enum pending/pass/fail) and defines `action_variance`, `object_displacement`, `continuity_score`, `contact_score`; video_sample.schema.yaml requires `video_id`, `filter_status` (enum pass/fail/error), `condition`, `generation_timestamp`. The plan (T3) and data-model reference only video_sample.schema.yaml; dataset_schema.schema.yaml is orphaned and contradicts it. Remove or reconcile it so contract tests validate against one SSoT.

Data-model states 'Five core entities, each with a contract schema under contracts/' but there is no `trained_model.schema.yaml` for the TrainedModel entity (fields model_id, condition, checkpoint_path, training_epochs, final_train_loss, training_duration_seconds, seed). Either add the schema or correct the data-model claim; T7/T8 produce checkpoints with no contract to validate them against.

Manifest locations disagree: plan puts curated/unfiltered manifests under `data/derived/curated/` and `data/derived/unfiltered/`; data-model puts them under `data/derived/manifests/` (curated_*.json, unfiltered_*.json). Pick one path so quickstart/CI and contract tests agree.

concerns.location: plan.md:Complexity Tracking vs spec.md:FR-001 and Assumptions
concerns.text: The plan replaces local Wan2.1 generation (FR-001, FR-010, FR-019 'identical Wan2.1 generation pipeline') with acquisition of pre-generated Wan2.1 videos from the Rapidata dataset. The plan itself flags this as a scope correction that 'should be reflected in the spec's assumption text', but spec.md still mandates generation. The spec's FR-001/FR-010/FR-019 wording and the Wan2.1-weights assumption must be updated to match the plan's dataset-acquisition approach, otherwise the plan contradicts the spec it implements.

The headline equivalence claim (filtered post-hoc curation ≈ PhysisForcing training-time optimization) is tested by comparing a ≈50M-param, 64×64, CPU-distilled model trained on ~100 videos against PUBLISHED PhysisForcing benchmark scores. The two systems differ in architecture, scale, resolution, training data, and compute — the filter is not the only varying factor. Any gap (or equivalence) is fully confounded; the design cannot answer the research question as stated. research.md acknowledges 'associational' framing, but SC-003/SC-004 still draw the comparable/not-comparable conclusion from this confounded comparison.

TOST requires two sample distributions. The PhysisForcing side is a single published aggregate score (T10: 'baseline scores from the published PhysisForcing results'), so a TOST with n≥64 per condition against it is undefined — you cannot compute a two-sample TOST against a point estimate with no variance. The plan must specify what the second sample actually is (e.g., per-video PhysisForcing scores, which are unavailable from a paper), or restrict TOST to the filtered-vs-unfiltered comparison only.

The Wilcoxon-Signed-Rank fallback is a PAIRED test, but the filtered vs unfiltered conditions are independent samples (different videos, separately trained models). A signed-rank test is the wrong non-parametric fallback here (Mann-Whitney/rank-based equivalence would be appropriate), and Wilcoxon signed-rank is not itself an equivalence procedure — no equivalence margin is defined for it. The spec mandates it, but the plan should flag/resolve this contradiction rather than propagate it.

No task samples/generates outputs from the trained diffusion models; T10 evaluates 'the filtered model' with no stated input videos. Without a generation step, the evaluation has no valid input and the n≥64 evaluation samples are undefined.

The curation rule conflates two different criteria: 'discard bottom filter_discard_percent (a percentile rule)' and 'raw score < 60 (an absolute threshold)'. These give different retained sets unless the 60th percentile happens to equal raw 60. The plan should state which rule is operative (and that the other is a sanity check), since the filtered/unfiltered contrast — the only causal comparison in the design — depends on it.

Power/construct concern: training a 50M-parameter video diffusion model for 10 epochs on ≤96 curated 64×64 videos on 2 CPU cores is very unlikely to produce a model whose generated videos are scoreable at all, making the downstream equivalence test vacuous. The plan needs a sanity gate (e.g., US-2 scenario 2's 80% MuJoCo pass rate) wired in as a go/no-go before TOST, or an acknowledgment of what a null result means.

FR-001/FR-010 mandate GENERATING videos with the Wan2.1 model; the plan substitutes acquisition of pre-existing Wan2.1 outputs from the Rapidata dataset. The plan itself concedes this 'should be reflected in the spec's assumption text' but the spec still says 'can be downloaded without requiring GPU resources for the generation step.'
